title: Aircraft Electrician (Acft Elec)
raw_text:
10-15F. MOS 15F--Aircraft Electrician (Acft Elec), CMF 15
     a. Major duties. The aircraft electrician performs and/or supervises inspections, repairs, maintenance
and testing according to drawings, blueprints, directives, technical manuals, and safety procedures of
aircraft electrical systems and electronic components to include associated subsystems by applying the
principles of electricity/electronics, hydrostatic motion, pneumatics, and hydraulics. Prepares aircraft
related maintenance forms and records. Typically assigned to Aviation Field or Sustainment maintenance
units.
Duties for MOS 15F at each level of skill are:
       (1) MOSC 15F1O. Diagnoses and troubleshoots malfunctions in electrical and electronic
components, including solid state and transistorized subsystems. Repairs aircraft instrument systems.
Applies principles of electricity/electronics, hydrostatic motion, pneumatics and hydraulics applicable to
repair aircraft instrument systems. Removes, installs, repairs, adjusts and tests electrical/electronic
elements of assemblies and components according to technical manuals, directives and safety
procedures. Clean, preserve and store electrical/electronic components and aircraft instruments.
Removes, repairs, services, installs, and troubleshoots nickel-cadmium batteries. Uses and performs
operator maintenance on ground support equipment, common and special tools. Maintains facilities for
storage of flammable and hazardous materials. Requisitions and maintains shop and bench stock for
repair of aircraft electrical systems and subsystems. Prepares request for turn-ins and repair parts for
electrical components. Prepares forms and records related to aircraft maintenance.
       (2) MOSC 15F2O. Performs duties described in paragraph (1) and provides technical guidance to
subordinate personnel. Diagnoses and troubleshoots malfunctions in aircraft electrical components and
their subcomponents. Participate in maintenance test flights as required. Monitors hazardous material
control and storage.
       (3) MOSC 15F3O. Supervises and provides technical guidance to subordinate personnel
performing duties described in paragraphs (1, 2) and evaluates the technical training program. Evaluate
maintenance operations and facilities for compliance with directives, technical manuals, work standards,
safety procedures and operational policies. Performs maintenance trend analysis and applies production
control, quality control and other maintenance management principles and procedures to aircraft electrical
system maintenance, nondestructive inspections and shop operations. Instructs personnel and conducts
technical training in aircraft electrical systems maintenance, nondestructive inspections, supply and safety
techniques. Monitors requisition of parts, tools, and supplies.
     b. Physical demands rating and qualifications for initial award or reclassification of MOS.
       (1) An aircraft electrician must possess the following qualifications: Waivers, and/or exceptions
must be approved by Cdr, AVCOE, ATTN: ATZQ-CDF-P, Ft Rucker, AL 36362-1100,
(https://home.army.mil/rucker/about/AVCOE/opfd/enlisted)
           (a) A physical demands rating of Moderate (Gold).
           (b) A physical profile of 222222.
           (c) Normal color vision.
           (d) Qualifying scores.
               (1) A minimum score of 104 in aptitude area MM.
               (2) A Minimum OPAT score of Standing Long Jump (LJ) -0120 cm, Seated Power Throw (PT)
         - 0350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) - 0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) - 0036 shuttles in
         Physical Demands Category “Moderate” (Gold).
            (e) Formal training (completion of a resident MOS 15F course conducted under the auspices of
The United States Army Aviation Center of Excellence (AVCOE).
            (f) Reclassification: Must meet the above qualifications and all prerequisites IAW AR 614-200
“Reclassification of primary military occupational specialty and/or secondary military occupational
specialty” chapter and AR 40-501 “Medical Fitness Standards for Retention and Separation, including
Retirement” chapter. Must be in the grade of SPC (non-promotable) or below unless they have held an
aviation maintenance/component repairer CMF 15 MOS for a minimum of 12 months at skill level 1 or 2,
18 months at skill level 3 or 24 months at skill level 4.
               1. Active Component: Soldiers that do not meet the above qualifications must submit a
determination packet to Cdr, AVCOE, ATTN: ATZQ-CDF-P, Ft Rucker, AL 36362-1100,
(https://home.army.mil/rucker/about/AVCOE/opfd/enlisted)
               2. National Guard: Soldiers that do not meet the above qualifications must submit a
determination packet through National Guard Bureau, ATTN: NGB-ARNG-AV, 111 South George Mason
Drive, Arlington, VA 22204-1382, (ng.ncr.ngb.mbx.avn-trng-mgt@army.mil).
              3. Reserve Component: Soldiers that do not meet the above qualifications must submit a
determination packet through Commander, Army Reserve Aviation Command (ARAC), ATTN: G3 (AFAK-
OPT), 1160 Brandenburg Station Road, Ft Knox, KY 40121-4190, (usarmy.usarc.arac.list.g-37-
training@army.mil).
       (2) MOS closed for reclassification to Soldiers who have been deemed permanently non-deployable
in accordance with AR 40-501, AR 220-1, AR 600-8-101, and AR 614-30. Soldiers must meet the
minimum criteria for retainability stated in AR 635-40, paragraph 3-5(a) and be fully deployable to all
locations and echelons.
     c. Additional skill identifiers. (Note: Refer to table 12-8 (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with all
enlisted MOS)).
     (1) A9--UH-60M Helicopter Qualification. (Rescind 202510).
     (2) Q2--Aviation Life Support Equipment (ALSE) personnel only.
     d. Physical requirements and standards of grade. Physical requirements and SG relating to each skill
level are listed in the following tables:
       (1) Table 10-15F-1. Physical requirements.
       (2) Table 10-15F-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
       (3) Table 10-15F-3. Standards of grade TDA.

Clean, maintain, and sterilize instruments or equipment.
Clean, preserve and store electrical/electronic components and aircraft instruments.

Prepare hazardous material for removal or storage.
Maintains facilities for storage of flammable and hazardous materials.

Maintain, repair, and rebuild aircraft structures, functional components, and parts, such as wings and fuselage, rigging, hydraulic units, oxygen systems, fuel systems, electrical systems, gaskets, or seals.
Requisitions and maintains shop and bench stock for repair of aircraft electrical systems and subsystems.

Inspect aircraft components to locate cracks, breaks, leaks, or other problems.
Diagnoses and troubleshoots malfunctions in aircraft electrical components and their subcomponents.
Construct and maintain test facilities for aircraft parts and systems, according to specifications.
Participate in maintenance test flights as required.
Monitor transportation and storage of flammable and other potentially dangerous products to ensure that safety guidelines are followed.
Monitors hazardous material control and storage.
Supervise or advise subordinate personnel.
Supervises and provides technical guidance to subordinate personnel performing duties described in paragraphs (1, 2) and evaluates the technical training program.
Develop, implement, or evaluate maintenance policies and procedures.
Evaluate maintenance operations and facilities for compliance with directives, technical manuals, work standards, safety procedures and operational policies.
Inspect work of aircraft mechanics performing maintenance, modification, or repair and overhaul of aircraft and aircraft mechanical systems to ensure adherence to standards and procedures.

Performs maintenance trend analysis and applies production control, quality control and other maintenance management principles and procedures to aircraft electrical system maintenance, nondestructive inspections and shop operations.
Analyze training programs and conduct oral and written examinations to ensure the competency of persons operating, installing, and repairing aircraft equipment.
Instructs personnel and conducts technical training in aircraft electrical systems maintenance, nondestructive inspections, supply and safety techniques.
Monitor, inspect, or test mechanical equipment.
Monitors requisition of parts, tools, and supplies.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
